drawer.context-hint: GoFiBot sees which page you are on.
drawer.history-empty: No conversations yet. The controller keeps them for about 12 hours.
drawer.history-gone: That conversation is no longer available; the controller keeps conversations for about 12 hours.
drawer.intro: Ask about this GoFi: its flows, CEL expressions, and Python libraries. GoFiBot reads the configuration, drafts changes, and can open the page you need.
drawer.placeholder: Ask GoFiBot… Enter or Ctrl+Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line
drawer.stop-max-tokens: The reply reached the length limit.
drawer.stop-max-tool-steps: Stopped at the tool step limit; ask it to continue.
drawer.title: GoFiBot
drawer.tool-approval-hint: The reply is paused until you decide; after two minutes the call is denied.
drawer.tool-call-expired: This call is no longer waiting (it timed out or was decided elsewhere).

highlight.flow-unavailable: The flow could not be loaded: {{message}}
highlight.unknown-block: No block named {{block}} in this flow.

proposal.expired-hint: It was already decided, or the server forgot it.
proposal.hint: Nothing is applied until you approve. Review the input first.

aria.edge-description: Press Enter or Space to select a connection, then Delete to remove it or Escape to cancel.
aria.node-description: Press Enter or Space to select a node. Press Delete to remove it and Escape to cancel.
aria.node-description-keyboard: Press Enter or Space to select a node, then use the arrow keys to move it. Press Delete to remove it and Escape to cancel.

broker-forms.ack-hint: Each message is acknowledged after its pipeline run returns (sinks included), so a crash or restart redelivers unacknowledged messages. Sink errors are logged, not retried. Credentials are stored inline in the flow for now.
broker-forms.ack-wait-description: Redelivered if the pipeline run takes longer; 1s to 1h.
broker-forms.amqp-description: RabbitMQ queue or exchange binding; acked after each delivery
broker-forms.amqp-url-description: amqp:// or amqps://, with the vhost as the path.
broker-forms.brokers-description: Seed brokers as host:port; press Enter after each.
broker-forms.channels-description: Pub/Sub keeps nothing while disconnected: at-most-once.
broker-forms.consumer-group-description: Defaults to gofi-<flow name>. Replicas in one group share partitions.
broker-forms.creds-file-description: Takes precedence over the other credentials. Same options as the NATS sink.
broker-forms.deliver-policy-description: Fixed when the consumer is first created.
broker-forms.durable-consumer-description: Defaults to gofi-<flow name>; created or updated.
broker-forms.exchange-description: Bound to a temporary, exclusive queue: each replica gets every message, and nothing is kept while disconnected.
broker-forms.field-description: Emit only this entry field. Leave blank for all fields as one JSON object.
broker-forms.group-description: Defaults to gofi-<flow name>; created if missing.
broker-forms.jetstream-description: Durable NATS JetStream consumer with explicit acks
broker-forms.kafka-description: Consumer group; offsets commit after each record
broker-forms.kafka-egress-hint: In a policy-managed cluster, egress is allowed to the seed brokers only; brokers the cluster advertises on other hosts need their own allowance.
broker-forms.queue-description: An existing queue. Replicas consuming it share its messages.
broker-forms.redis-description: Stream consumer group (XACK) or Pub/Sub channels
broker-forms.redis-url-description: redis:// or rediss://, with the database as the path.
broker-forms.start-offset-description: Only for a group with no committed offset; afterwards the group resumes where it left off.
broker-forms.tls-pair: Set both certificate and key, or neither.

broker-validation.topic-name: "{{topic}}" is not a valid topic name.

codec-list-editor.decode-snappy: Decompress Snappy (block format, as in Prometheus remote write)
codec-list-editor.decode-zlib: Decompress zlib (deflate with a zlib header)
codec-list-editor.encode-zlib: Compress with zlib (deflate with a zlib header)
codec-list-editor.python-decoders-hint: Python decoders appear here once a library registering @gofi.decoder is launched.
codec-list-editor.python-encoders-hint: Python encoders appear here once a library registering @gofi.encoder is launched.

convert.branch: flow has a branch at "{{node}}" — a stage's outputs must be a single linear hop
convert.deadletter-incoming: only an Encode step can connect to the dead-letter sink: it receives the messages the flow rejects
convert.deadletter-multiple: the dead-letter sink can be connected from one Encode step only
convert.encode-detached: the Encode step feeding a sink must itself be connected from the last stage
convert.encode-outgoing: an Encode step can only connect to sinks
convert.mixed-targets: node "{{node}}" has a mix of stage and sink targets — a stage's outputs must all be stages or all be sinks, not both
convert.no-outgoing: flow is broken: node "{{node}}" has no outgoing connection to a sink
convert.sink-multiple-incoming: a sink is connected more than once: connect it from the last stage or from one Encode step
convert.sink-outgoing: sink nodes cannot have outgoing connections
convert.sink-required: at least one sink is required
convert.step-disconnected: the {{step}} step must be connected directly after the source (source, frame, decode, parse)
convert.step-order: {{step}} must come after {{previous}}: the order is source, frame, decode, parse
convert.unknown-node: flow references unknown node "{{node}}" between ingress and the sinks

exposure-settings.add-listener: Add a listener for this flow
exposure-settings.address-pool-description: MetalLB pool the address is taken from.
exposure-settings.allowed-senders-any: Any namespace may send. Choose network policy Package workloads to allow only them.
exposure-settings.allowed-senders-restricted: Only these network policy Package workloads may send; GoFi allows exactly them, and the Connectivity tab checks each sender's Package allows the egress.
exposure-settings.choose-envoy-gateway: Choose an Envoy Gateway Gateway for {{routeKind}}s.
exposure-settings.external-traffic-policy-description: Local keeps the sender's source IP (useful for UDP), but only nodes running the flow Pod accept traffic.
exposure-settings.gateway-description: A TCPRoute/UDPRoute on a Gateway listener (Envoy Gateway, Istio)
exposure-settings.gateway-port-description: Port the new listener opens on the Gateway address.
exposure-settings.internal-description: Pod port only, reachable where network policy allows
exposure-settings.listener-managed-description: Use an existing listener, or let GoFi add one for this flow.
exposure-settings.listener-same-namespace: This listener only accepts routes from its own namespace
exposure-settings.listener-same-namespace-fix: Set allowedRoutes to include namespace {{namespace}}, or let GoFi add a listener.
exposure-settings.listener-unmanaged-description: GoFi may not add listeners here (chart gateway.manageListeners); pick an existing one.
exposure-settings.load-balancer-class-description: Leave on the default unless several load balancer implementations run in this cluster.
exposure-settings.load-balancer-default-description: The cluster default load balancer serves this Service.
exposure-settings.load-balancer-description: An external address on any port, such as 60084
exposure-settings.no-gateways: No Gateways found. Create one with Envoy Gateway or Istio first.
exposure-settings.no-load-balancer: No load balancer detected in this cluster
exposure-settings.node-port-field-description: External port on every node, {{min}}–{{max}}. Leave blank to have Kubernetes assign one.
exposure-settings.node-port-range: This cluster accepts NodePorts {{min}}–{{max}}. For another port, use LoadBalancer or a Gateway route.
exposure-settings.requested-address-description: A specific IP from the pool (MetalLB metallb.io/loadBalancerIPs).
exposure-settings.service-annotations-description: For load balancer or platform integrations (for example kube-vip or cloud provider settings).
exposure-settings.uds-allow-managed: GoFi adds the network allow for this exposure to its gofi-flows network policy Package.
exposure-settings.uds-allow-unmanaged: The cluster's network policy blocks this ingress unless a Package allows it. Enable managed allows in the chart (uds.manageAllows), or add an allow for this port.

flow-canvas.name-format: Use lowercase letters, numbers, "-" or ".", starting and ending with a letter or number.
flow-canvas.name-required: Enter a name for this flow.
flow-canvas.saved-with-warnings_one: Saved, but a path is not allowed
flow-canvas.saved-with-warnings_other: Saved, but {{n}} paths are not allowed

flow-settings.default-library-description: Python framers, decoders, parsers, stages, and sinks that don't name a library run in this one.
flow-settings.title: Flow settings
flow-settings.usage-default: Functions you pick from {{library}} omit the library.
flow-settings.usage-refs_one: {{n}} Python function in this flow uses {{library}}. Removing the default writes it into them.
flow-settings.usage-refs_other: {{n}} Python functions in this flow use {{library}}. Removing the default writes it into them.

mock-panel.generate-tooltip: Generate a heuristic placeholder sample from the pipeline's expressions
mock-panel.title: Test flow

node-inspector.aster-hint: Send through an Aster agent in this workload's network namespace. Its API must stay on loopback.
node-inspector.aster-logical-key-field: Logical key field (instead of static key)
node-inspector.binary-mode-hint: In binary mode the flow binds a local TCP/UDP port.
node-inspector.cel-filter-hint: A true result keeps the message. Use fields for parsed data, meta for metadata, and raw for the original frame.
node-inspector.container-mode-hint: Container flows bind a TCP/UDP port. Publish it through your container runtime.
node-inspector.decode-hint: Decoders run top to bottom before parsing. For base64-encoded gzip data, add base64 first, then gzip. Python decoders (@gofi.decoder) can unwrap or decrypt. The raw frame is kept for inspection and replay.
node-inspector.decoded-size-limit-description: Each decoding step's output is capped at this size.
node-inspector.delimiter-appended-description: Use a direct destination address or select matching Kubernetes pods. The delimiter is appended to each forwarded message.
node-inspector.disconnect-dead-letter: Disconnect: the dead letter keeps its default payload
node-inspector.disconnect-sink: Disconnect: the sink keeps its default payload
node-inspector.encode-feeds-none: None yet. Connect a sink from this step, or choose it in a sink's Encoding field. An Encode step that feeds no sink is ignored when saving.
node-inspector.encode-node-hint: Serializes each message, then applies the encoders in order, for every sink connected from this step. Connect a sink here (or pick this step in its Encoding field) to encode it; a sink connected from the last stage directly keeps its default payload.
node-inspector.encode-wrapped-description: JSON with id, fields, and meta
node-inspector.encoding-description: An Encode step on the canvas serializes the message and applies encoders before this sink sends it; several sinks can share one. None keeps the sink's default payload.
node-inspector.error-continue-description: Continue and record the parse error
node-inspector.error-drop-description: Drop and send to the dead-letter sink
node-inspector.frame-hint: How the incoming byte stream becomes discrete frames. UDP datagrams are independent frames; line and delimiter framing can still split a datagram.
node-inspector.into-description: Field to hold the result. Empty merges at the top level.
node-inspector.listen-hint: Listen: senders connect to a GoFi TCP/UDP port.
node-inspector.loki-labels-description: The app=gofi and listener labels are included by default. Use a Loki base URL or its push endpoint.
node-inspector.mode-merge-description: Parsed fields are added to {{target}}; other fields are kept.
node-inspector.mode-merge-option-description: Add the parsed fields, keeping the others
node-inspector.mode-replace-description: The parsed result becomes the message fields.
node-inspector.mode-replace-option-description: The parsed result replaces all fields
node-inspector.no-decoders: No decoders: frames reach the parser unchanged.
node-inspector.no-decoders-parse-field: No decoders: the value is parsed as is.
node-inspector.no-encoders: No encoders: the formatted payload is sent as is.
node-inspector.on-error-continue-description: A value that fails to decode or parse leaves the message unchanged.
node-inspector.on-error-drop-description: A value that fails to decode or parse drops the message (and sends it to the dead-letter sink, if configured).
node-inspector.parse-field-hint: Parses a value into fields mid-pipeline, for example a JSON string carried inside an already-parsed message.
node-inspector.parse-from-cel-description: CEL expression for the value to parse.
node-inspector.parse-from-raw-description: Empty parses the raw frame (after the flow's decoders).
node-inspector.parse-hint: How a decoded frame becomes structured fields for stages and destinations. To parse a field again later (for example a JSON string inside an XML event), add a Parse field stage.
node-inspector.port-description-gateway: Port the Gateway forwards to (the in-cluster Service).
node-inspector.port-description-internal: Senders inside the cluster connect to the flow Pod on this port; no Service is created.
node-inspector.port-description-load-balancer: Port on the load balancer address (and the in-cluster Service).
node-inspector.port-description-node-port: In-cluster Service port. Senders outside the cluster use the NodePort.
node-inspector.port-description-service: Senders inside the cluster connect to the Service on this port.
node-inspector.python-framer-hint: The framer is called after each read with the buffered bytes and returns complete frames plus the remainder; at the end of the stream it is called once more with final=True.
node-inspector.python-framers-hint: Python framers (@gofi.framer) appear here once a library registering one is launched.
node-inspector.python-parsers-hint: Python parsers (@gofi.parser) appear here once a library registering one is launched.
node-inspector.python-sink-hint: This sink executes in GoFi's separate Python worker.
node-inspector.quic-hint: QUIC runs over UDP on this port (published as UDP everywhere) and always uses TLS: give the listener a certificate and key.
node-inspector.regex-hint: Matching messages continue. Use a parsed string field or match the original frame.
node-inspector.test-before-deploying: Test an example in Test flow before deploying.

options.source-fetch-description: Poll an HTTP endpoint on an interval
options.source-listen-description: Senders connect to a GoFi TCP/UDP port
options.source-python-description: A @gofi.fetcher or @gofi.streamer in an isolated library worker
options.source-subscribe-description: NATS, MQTT, WebSocket, SSE, Zenoh, Kafka, AMQP, JetStream, or Redis

pipeline-nodes.encode-no-encoders: No encoders: the formatted payload is sent as is
pipeline-nodes.encode-unconnected: Not connected to a sink: ignored when saving
pipeline-nodes.frame-raw: whole connection or datagram is one frame

python-source.config-object: Config must be a JSON object, e.g. {"limit": 10}.
python-source.every-format: Use a duration such as 10s, 1m, or 1m30s.
python-source.not-registered: Not registered as a fetcher or streamer by a ready worker
python-source.wrong-kind: {{library}}.{{function}} is a {{kind}}; a source needs @gofi.fetcher or @gofi.streamer.

python-source-form.add-library-hint: Add one in <1>Functions</1>: <3>New function</3> offers Fetcher and Streamer templates. Save and launch the library so its worker registers them.
python-source-form.config-description: Passed to the function as keyword arguments.
python-source-form.every-description: Poll interval for a fetcher. Empty uses the decorator's every, else 30s. Each call runs under the library's timeout.
python-source-form.every-description-with-default: Poll interval for a fetcher. Empty uses the decorator's every ({{every}}), else 30s. Each call runs under the library's timeout.
python-source-form.fetcher-description: Fetcher: called every interval; calls never overlap.
python-source-form.library-description: Saved libraries that register a @gofi.fetcher or @gofi.streamer.
python-source-form.no-source-library: No ready library registers a fetcher or streamer
python-source-form.streamer-description: Streamer: kept running; restarted with backoff if it fails.

python-templates.ai-classify-description: Have the AI pick one label from a list, then drop or route by it; needs the AI endpoint enabled for functions under Administration
python-templates.ai-enrich-description: Ask the AI about each message and add its answer as a field; needs the AI endpoint enabled for functions under Administration
python-templates.ai-extract-description: Pull the values of a pydantic model out of each message into a field; needs the AI endpoint enabled for functions under Administration
python-templates.ai-sink-description: Let the AI triage each delivered message and pick an action; your code carries it out. Needs the AI endpoint enabled for functions under Administration
python-templates.binary-description: Fixed-layout binary frames with struct or construct
python-templates.encoder-description: bytes → bytes before a sink sends (Encode step)
python-templates.expected-drop: expected the message to be dropped
python-templates.fetcher-description: Poll on an interval as a flow source; needs egress rules for network access
python-templates.framer-description: Split a byte stream into frames (Frame step)
python-templates.pydantic-description: Declare the frame shape as a model; frames that do not match are dropped
python-templates.sink-description: Print-only unless the library has egress rules
python-templates.streamer-description: Yield frames continuously as a flow source

s3-form.after-keep-description: In-memory cursor: a restart re-reads the prefix unless Since is set
s3-form.after-move-description: Move each object under another prefix after hand-off (at-least-once)
s3-form.credentials-hint: Leave the keys blank to use ambient credentials (AWS_* environment, IRSA web identity, or instance metadata). Inline keys are stored in the flow definition.
s3-form.endpoint-description: Leave blank for AWS S3. For MinIO, Ceph, or GCS interop use e.g. https://minio.example:9000.
s3-form.key-glob-description: Matched after the prefix; * does not cross /.
s3-form.key-pair-problem: Set both keys, or neither for ambient credentials.
s3-form.move-prefix-problem: Use a prefix outside the watched prefix, e.g. done/.
s3-form.path-style-description: Usually required by MinIO and Ceph.
s3-form.since-description: Skip objects last modified at or before this time.
s3-form.split-description: One frame per element of a JSON array in each object, e.g. $[*]. For one frame per line, use line framing instead.

sink-target-tools.delivery-all-description: Every matching ready Pod receives each message (replay to all).
sink-target-tools.delivery-one-description: Each message goes to one matching Pod, load-balanced.
sink-target-tools.egress-allow-added: GoFi adds the egress allow to its network policy Package.
sink-target-tools.ingress-allow-needed: The target namespace must also allow ingress from {{namespace}} on this port (an Ingress allow with remoteNamespace {{remoteNamespace}} in a policy-managed cluster).
sink-target-tools.namespace-cluster-wide: Pods in other namespaces are reached through a GoFi-managed EndpointSlice in {{namespace}}.
sink-target-tools.namespace-local-only: GoFi namespace only: cluster discovery is disabled (chart discovery.clusterWide).
sink-target-tools.pick-package: Pick from a network policy Package
sink-target-tools.pick-package-description: Workloads other Packages expose or admit on {{transport}}. Fills namespace, labels, and port; the Connectivity tab verifies the Package admits GoFi.
sink-target-tools.send-sample-description: Sends real {{network}} traffic directly to {{target}}. Include any framing delimiter in the payload.
sink-target-tools.socket-write-caveat: A successful socket write does not confirm application processing.

source-settings.fetch-s3-description: New objects in a bucket prefix (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph, GCS interop)
source-settings.fetch-sql-description: Rows from a PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQL Server query
source-settings.mqtt-topic-description: Wildcards: + matches one level, # the rest.
source-settings.nats-creds-description: Takes precedence over the other credentials. TLS options are shared with the NATS sink.
source-settings.nats-description: Core NATS subject, optional queue group
source-settings.nats-subject-description: Wildcards: * matches one token, > the rest.
source-settings.pulled-source-hint: Each {{unit}} enters Frame as its own stream; keep Frame on Raw for one frame per message. The flow runtime connects outward, so in a policy-managed cluster add an egress allowance for this endpoint.
source-settings.python-source-hint: Each frame the function returns or yields enters Frame as its own stream; a dict becomes one JSON frame. The function runs in the library's isolated worker, never in the flow runtime or the controller: its network access is the library's egress allowlist (Functions › Network), and this flow needs no egress allowance of its own.
source-settings.queue-group-description: Replicas in the same group share messages instead of each receiving all.
source-settings.send-after-connecting-description: A text message such as a subscription request.
source-settings.split-http-description: One frame per element of a JSON array, e.g. $.items[*]. Leave blank for one frame per response.
source-settings.sse-description: Each Server-Sent Event is one frame
source-settings.sse-reconnect-description: Reconnects resend Last-Event-ID so the server can resume.
source-settings.subject: Subject
source-settings.zenoh-description: Key expression through the router REST plugin; each sample is one frame

sql-form.cursor-column-description: A unique, increasing column such as id.
sql-form.dsn-description: The driver's own connection string. It usually contains the password and is stored in the flow definition.
sql-form.query-cursor-hint: Bind the last cursor value with {{placeholder}} and ORDER BY {{column}}.
sql-form.query-description: Each row becomes one JSON object frame.
sql-form.query-no-cursor-hint: Without a cursor column every poll re-reads the same rows.
sql-form.read-only-hint: PostgreSQL and MySQL polls run in a read-only transaction and GoFi rejects obvious write statements, but neither is a security boundary: connect as a database user that can only read.
sql-form.start-after-description: An integer, RFC 3339 time, or text.

stage-palette.add-sink-card-description: Forward passing traffic to an application.
stage-palette.add-sink-menu-description: Forward passing traffic to an application
stage-palette.card-title: Click to add, or drag onto a connection
stage-palette.cel-filter-description: Drop messages failing a CEL boolean expression
stage-palette.dead-letter-search-terms: Dead letter sink rejected dropped messages destination
stage-palette.dedup-description: Drop repeats of a key seen within a time window
stage-palette.encode-card-description: Format and encode messages before a sink sends them. Drop it on a sink's connection, or wire sinks to it.
stage-palette.encode-menu-description: Format and encode messages before a sink sends them
stage-palette.encode-search-terms: Encode encoding format wrapped fields raw encoder gzip base64 compress payload before sink
stage-palette.inline-python-description: Write a Python transformer directly in this flow
stage-palette.launch-library-hint: Launch a Python library to add its transformer functions here.
stage-palette.parse-field-description: Parse a field again (JSON, XML, text, or Python)
stage-palette.rate-limit-description: Drop messages exceeding a per-second rate
stage-palette.regex-filter-description: Match raw traffic or a parsed field with RE2
stage-palette.sink-search-terms: Add sink destination forward HTTP NATS TCP UDP Aster Zenoh Loki stdout container application
stage-palette.step-decode-description: Apply byte decoders in order (base64, gzip, hex…). Without it, frames are not decoded.
stage-palette.step-frame-description: Split the byte stream into frames (line, delimiter, length prefix). Without it, each connection or datagram is one frame.
stage-palette.step-parse-description: Turn frames into fields (JSON, XML, text, or a Python parser). Without it, frames pass through as fields.raw.
stage-palette.title: Add a stage
stage-palette.transform-description: Set, rename, or remove a field

tls.alpn-description: Application protocols offered in the handshake; empty means {{alpn}}.
tls.ca-listen-description: Client certificates are verified against this CA when required below.
tls.ca-sink-description: The server certificate is verified against this CA; empty uses the system roots.
tls.require-client-cert-description: Only senders presenting a certificate signed by the CA may connect (mTLS).
tls.server-cert-description: PEM certificate the listener presents; senders verify it against their CA.
tls.server-name-description: Name expected in the server certificate when it differs from the URL host.

validation.bucket-format: Use 3–63 lowercase letters, digits, dots, or hyphens.
validation.duration-format: Use a duration such as 500ms, 10s, 5m, or 1h.
validation.rfc3339-format: Use an RFC 3339 time such as 2026-01-02T15:04:05Z.
validation.split-format: Use $[*] or a path such as $.items[*].
validation.sql-bind-cursor: Bind the cursor value with {{placeholder}} and ORDER BY {{column}}.
validation.sql-read-only: Use a read-only query (SELECT or WITH).

zenoh-form.key-expression-description: * matches one chunk, ** any number. Each sample is one frame; meta carries zenoh.key, zenoh.kind, zenoh.encoding, and zenoh.timestamp.
zenoh-form.read-stored-values-description: Also query the router's storages for current values each time the subscription (re)connects. A value may arrive twice.
zenoh-form.router-url-description: The Zenoh router's REST plugin origin (port 8000 by default).
zenoh-form.sample-kinds-description: A DELETE sample has no value; its frame is {"key", "kind", "timestamp"}.
zenoh-form.sent-with-hint: Sent with HTTP {{operation}} through the router's REST plugin; enable the plugin on your router.
zenoh-form.zenoh-key-description: One concrete key; wildcards and @ admin paths are rejected.

zenoh-validation.key-concrete: Use a concrete key without wildcards, query syntax, or @ admin paths.
zenoh-validation.key-no-wildcards: Use one concrete key without wildcards.
zenoh-validation.key-segments: Segments must be nonempty and cannot be . or ..
zenoh-validation.key-whole-wildcards: Wildcards must be whole * or ** segments; @ (admin space) and query syntax are not allowed.
zenoh-validation.origin-absolute: Enter an absolute URL such as http://zenoh-router:8000.
zenoh-validation.origin-credentials: Put credentials under Authentication, not in the URL.
zenoh-validation.origin-only: Use the origin only, without a path or query.
zenoh-validation.origin-scheme: Use the router REST origin, http:// or https:// (not the native 7447 port).

field.entry-missing: This library entry does not exist.
field.latest-tooltip: Follows the latest generation: library edits reload this flow.
field.pinned-tooltip: Pinned: later library edits do not reach this stage.
field.unlink-tooltip: Copy the current text into this stage and stop following the library

on-error.drop-description: Errors drop the message (and send it to the dead-letter sink, if configured).
on-error.label: On evaluation error
on-error.pass-description: Errors let the message continue unchanged (fail open).

picker.bool-only: Only bool expressions can be used here.
picker.create-hint: Create entries on the CEL library page.
picker.intro: Link keeps this stage in sync with the library entry. Insert copies its current text.
picker.search-placeholder: Search name, description, expression, or tag
picker.title: CEL library

connectivity.header-blocked: {{paths}} this flow needs outside namespace {{namespace}} · {{blocked}} blocked.
connectivity.kubernetes-only-body: Connectivity checks verify network policy Packages and policies in a cluster.
connectivity.not-allowed-body-applicable: GoFi tried to send and failed, and a network policy Package does not allow the path. GoFi can update its own Package: review the change before applying it.
connectivity.not-allowed-body-owner: GoFi tried to send and failed, and a network policy Package does not allow the path. The Package belongs to the application on the other side; expand the path for the entry its owner needs to add.
connectivity.nothing-to-verify-body: This flow only talks inside namespace {{namespace}}, which GoFi's Package already allows.
connectivity.python-source-body: The source function executes in that library's isolated worker, not in this flow's runtime, so its outbound traffic is not a path of this flow. Allow its destinations with the library's egress rules (Functions › {{library}} › Network). This flow only calls the worker inside namespace {{namespace}}.
connectivity.unreachable-body_one: The Packages allow this path, yet sends fail. Check that the destination is up and that nothing outside Kubernetes (a firewall, DNS) is in the way.
connectivity.unreachable-body_other: The Packages allow these paths, yet sends fail. Check that the destination is up and that nothing outside Kubernetes (a firewall, DNS) is in the way.
connectivity.unreachable-title_one: {{count}} route fails, but not because of network policy
connectivity.unreachable-title_other: {{count}} routes fail, but not because of network policy

flow-yaml-editor.intro: The {{apiVersion}} Flow resource and its live graph: edit either side.
flow-yaml-editor.rename-refused: metadata.name must stay "{{name}}"; create a new flow to use another name
flow-yaml-editor.saved-with-warnings_one: Saved, but a path is not allowed
flow-yaml-editor.saved-with-warnings_other: Saved, but {{count}} paths are not allowed

administration.allow-changes-description: When on, the assistant can propose creating or replacing flows, CEL expressions, and Python libraries; each proposal is applied only when a user approves it in the chat. Off: it only reads, validates, and drafts.
administration.allow-functions: Functions may use the AI endpoint
administration.allow-functions-description: When on, every Python library can call this model through gofi.llm via the controller; the key never reaches a worker, and each call is checked here. Off: gofi.llm raises in every library. One switch for the deployment; libraries have no setting of their own.
administration.api-key-environment: The current key comes from the environment. Leaving this empty keeps it; a key entered here is stored and takes precedence.
administration.api-key-none: No key is set. Enter one to enable the assistant.
administration.api-key-stored: A key is stored. Leaving this empty keeps the stored key.
administration.assistant-card-description: GoFiBot: model endpoint, API key, what it may change, and the tools it is offered.
administration.assistant-intro: GoFiBot answers questions about this GoFi and drafts flows, CEL expressions, and Python libraries through a model endpoint: the Anthropic Messages API or any OpenAI-compatible service.

administration.check-failed-unknown: The endpoint did not answer as expected.

administration.enabled-description: Shows the chat control in the header once a working endpoint answers.
administration.instructions-description: Appended to the system prompt: house rules, naming conventions, what to avoid.
administration.instructions-placeholder: Always name flows after the producing team. Never suggest NodePort exposure.

ingress.docker-text: Each flow is a container that publishes its port one-to-one on the Docker host, so senders use the Docker host's address with the flow's port. Containers on the shared GoFi network can use the flow container's name instead.
ingress.host-text: Each flow binds its port directly on the machine running GoFi, so senders use that machine's address with the flow's port (127.0.0.1 from the same machine). Kubernetes exposure settings do not apply here.
ingress.in-cluster: From inside the cluster, send to the flow's Service instead:
ingress.kubernetes-text: Each flow is a Pod with its own Service. How far the port reaches is the flow's exposure: Internal or ClusterIP (inside the cluster), NodePort (a port between {{min}} and {{max}} on every node), LoadBalancer (an external address), or a Gateway route (TCPRoute/UDPRoute on a Gateway listener).
ingress.kubernetes-where: Set it in the flow editor: select the source node, then Exposure in the inspector. The Connections page lists the addresses the cluster assigned.
ingress.no-flow: No flow is saved yet; the command below targets the example from the previous step.
ingress.placeholders: Replace the values in angle brackets with your cluster's: a node or load-balancer address, and the NodePort shown on the flow once it is saved.
ingress.port-forward: With no exposure, reach the flow from your workstation through a port-forward to its Pod, then send to the forwarded port:
ingress.quic: This flow listens on QUIC, which netcat cannot speak; see the QUIC guide for a client.
ingress.send-text: Send one test frame from a terminal (the trailing newline completes the line frame):

monitoring.dashboard-text: Import docs/grafana-dashboard.json for traffic, parser errors, rejections, sink failures, latency, and Loki logs; pick your data sources after import.
monitoring.explore: Live traffic from all flows or one. Search fields and raw bytes; filter by level and by accepted or rejected.
monitoring.intro: Now send the test frame and watch it arrive. Live views are bounded and best effort: they show what flows see right now, not durable history.
monitoring.live-traffic-text: One flow's messages with the inspector: parsed fields, metadata, and which stage rejected a message.
monitoring.logs: GoFi itself logs one JSON object per line on stdout, and the stdout sink prints each message there too.
monitoring.metrics-text: Scrape {{url}}: frames received, parse errors, rejected messages, sink dispatches and latency, each labelled with the flow name.
monitoring.problems-text: Runtime problems per component (source, parser, stage, sink) with counts and when they last happened; also a badge in the top bar.

navigation.administration: Configuration export, deployment details, and GoFiBot settings.
navigation.cel: Saved CEL expressions that stages reuse by name.
navigation.cluster: The namespace GoFi runs in: Pods, packages, and the network policies that affect flows.
navigation.connections: Endpoints GoFi discovered (Services, Pods, containers) to pick as destinations.
navigation.explore: Live traffic from all flows at once, searchable and filterable.
navigation.flows: Every flow; open one to edit its pipeline, watch its traffic, and read its problems.
navigation.functions: Python function libraries (framers, parsers, transformers, sinks) that run in isolated workers.
navigation.intro: The main menu on the left (the bars button opens it on small screens) holds every tool:
navigation.tips: The search box in the top bar (Ctrl+K or ⌘K) jumps to any page or flow. The badge at the bottom of the menu shows how this GoFi is deployed.

welcome.decode-text: Decoders such as base64 or gzip unwrap the frame; the parser (JSON, XML, text, Python) turns it into fields.
welcome.encode-text: Format and encoders before a sink sends: wrapped, fields or raw, then gzip, base64 or a Python encoder. Several sinks can share one.
welcome.frames-text: Bytes become messages: one per line, per delimiter, per length prefix, or per connection.
welcome.intro: GoFi connects data that arrives in odd or unknown shapes to the applications that need it. A flow is the whole path: where data comes in, how it is cut into messages and understood, what is kept, and where it goes.
welcome.live: Everything a flow sees shows up live in this portal. Home, behind this panel, lists every flow and its traffic.
welcome.sinks-text: HTTP, TCP, UDP, NATS, Loki, stdout and more receive the result; a dead-letter sink gets what was rejected.
welcome.source-text: Where data arrives: a TCP or UDP port GoFi listens on, or an endpoint it polls or subscribes to.
welcome.stages-text: CEL and regex filters, transforms, schema checks, deduplication and rate limits decide what passes and reshape it.
